items.about: BIRAC's PCP Fund helps Indian biotech startups with a market-ready product (TRL 7+) pay for the final push to launch — market testing, scale-up and commercial roll-out. It is soft funding repaid through a royalty, not a free grant, so it suits teams expecting revenue within 6–18 months. The catch: BIRAC's contribution is repaid as a royalty within 5 years of project completion — 1.5x if the product is commercialised, 1x if not, with at least 20% paid each year. Keep ready the incorporation certificate, CA/CS shareholding certificate with UDIN and passports of the 51% Indian shareholders.
items.eligibility:
Indian startup incorporated within the last 10 years (as per the incorporation certificate)
At least 51% Indian shareholding held by Indian citizens, certified by a CA/CS with a valid UDIN
Product or technology at TRL 7 or above on BIRAC's scale and of national relevance — it need not have been developed with BIRAC money
Applicant must put in at least 30% of the total project cost
A product that has already received PCP funding cannot apply again
items.benefits:
BIRAC co-funds the cost of taking a validated product to market (launch, market testing, scale-up)
No equity taken — repayment is via royalty
Milestone-linked fund releases with committee guidance on commercial readiness
Route for products from BIRAC's BIG/SBIRI/BioNEST pipeline as well as externally funded biotech startups

items.about: A $50 million global grant programme for teams that partner with a city to deploy AI that improves public services for underserved residents — in health, economic mobility, environmental resilience or civic services. Indian non-profits, public benefit companies and, in limited cases, for-profit startups can apply if they have a city government on board. Round 1 closes 29 November 2026 at 11:59 pm US Eastern (about 10:29 am IST on 30 November) on the citiesdeliver.rockefellerfoundation.org portal. Round 1 needs an eligibility screen, a short video demo of the AI solution, a certificate of incorporation (or 501(c)(3)-equivalency/fiscal-sponsor proof) and a city partner's letter of intent — getting the city letter is the real bottleneck, so start now. Shortlisted teams interview in January 2027 and submit full proposals by 1 March 2027. For-profit applicants cannot claim indirect costs.
items.eligibility:
Lead applicant must be a non-profit (including university labs and fiscally sponsored groups), a public benefit corporation, or a for-profit company whose project is charitable and benefits the business only incidentally
Must have a city partner — a city of 50,000+ residents with its own municipal government — that provides a letter of intent; governments cannot apply directly
Project must use AI to improve access to or quality of public services for poor, vulnerable or underserved communities in public health, economic mobility, environmental resilience or civic engagement (election/voting projects excluded)
Open globally including India; organisations in countries under comprehensive US OFAC sanctions are excluded
For-profits must disclose their business model, show an open-source approach for lasting public benefit, and ring-fence grant funds
items.benefits:
Seed track: $500,000 to under $1 million for early concepts ready for a first city pilot
Scale track: $1–2 million for solutions already piloted in a city with early results
24-month grant, half paid upfront and half after a mid-term milestone
No equity taken
Visibility within a global cohort backed by the Rockefeller and OpenAI foundations
